title: Best Aniimo Starter To Choose: Helion Or Lunara
description: Aniimo has been released as a new free-to-play creature-catching game similar to Palworld and Pokemon. Early in the storyline, the game asks you to make a major decision in choosing from one of two "starter" Aniimo as a guardian. In this guide, we'll discuss the differences between these two Aniimo, so you can make the best choice for your playthrough. Who are Helion and Lunara? Helion and Lunara evolutions You'll encounter two talking Aniimo called Helion and Lunara, who appear to be essential to the game's story and also act as a guardian for your time in the world of Idyll. Only one can accompany you on your journey, at least for now anyway. The story suggests you can reunite with the other Aniimo later in the game, but it's uncertain if they'll be able to join your party. Which Aniimo should you choose? Helion and Lunara comparison There are different ways to approach your choice, as neither Aniimo is a bad option. Maybe you think one Aniimo looks or sounds cuter, and you want it to be your companion for the game. They both look and sound adorable, but Helion looks like a fiery lion cub, and Lunara is a blue and white fox. If you want to think in terms of gameplay strategy, here's a breakdown of the two choices: Both Helion and Lunara are DPS-based, have the same stats, and share the Light elemental type. The biggest difference between the two is going to be their attack styles. Helion will be the best choice if you want close-range, melee-type burst attacks, and Lunara is a great pick if you want to fight with range-based attacks. Again, the two Aniimo are very similar in all ways except visuals and combat style. Lunara might also be the most beginner-friendly pick, as she allows you to fight from a safer distance. Ultimately, the choice is yours. We'll also provide an update if there is a way to later unlock the Aniimo you don't choose for your adventure.

title: New PS5 Update Is Out Now, And Sony Actually Added Some New Features
description: A new PS5 firmware update has arrived, and it's upgrading the console with more than just extra stability. Firmware update version 26.06-14.00.00 offers a new tweak for the PS5 Pro console, voice chat improvements, and tweaks to longstanding features. Here's a breakdown of everything. For PS5 Pro owners, the update will now see the option for enhanced PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) turned on by default. When this is active, it will allow games to run with sharper, smoother visuals, and it also works with games that support the previous version of PSSR. If you're feeling social, you can also see who's talking when a voice chat group is active--which should come in very handy for games like Big Walk. You'll need to turn this option on, but it's easy to do, and the instructions are listed below. Additionally, new widgets have been added to the home screen. These include a trending tab for new game releases or games with major content updates, as well as multiplayer games and popular multiplayer modes. Bluetooth features for PS5 consoles have been changed depending on which country you reside in, and to cap things off, system software performance and stability have been further improved. This is easily the biggest PS5 firmware update since March, when PS5 Pro consoles received the enhanced version of PSSR. This week's enhancements arrive ahead of a very busy gaming season, as the PS5 exclusive Marvel's Wolverine has launched and other big games on the horizon include Control Resonant, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and Grand Theft Auto 6. PS5 Version 26.06-14.00.00 Update Notes We've turned on Enhance PSSR Image Quality as a default setting. When you update the system software, this setting automatically turns on. When you enable this feature, enhanced PSSR is used even for games that support the previous version of PSSR, so you can enjoy a sharper and clearer visual experience. title: Wo Long 2: Wings Of Ember Made Me Rethink My Relationship With Soulslikes
description: I went into my hands-on session with Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember expecting to hate it. That probably isn't the sort of sentence Team Ninja wants associated with its upcoming action-RPG, but it's an important one. I've never been great at souls-likes. The combination of punishing enemies, precise timing, complicated combat systems, and the possibility that something resembling an eldritch horror might annihilate me in three hits is not my idea of a fun time. Wo Long 2 initially looked like it was going to be another game determined to make me suffer. Instead, I had a surprisingly great time and walked away from my Gamescom preview eager to play more. The sequel to 2023's Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty is still built around fast, demanding martial-arts combat, with deflection remaining a crucial part of surviving encounters. After my demo, I went back and played the original, and found it to be far more approachable than I remembered. However, Team Ninja has made some significant changes since Fallen Dynasty that mean I can already confidently say that Wings of Ember feels like a far superior game to its predecessor. My problem with souls-likes isn't necessarily that they're difficult; it's that they refuse to explain themselves. That's great for gamers who enjoy throwing themselves at things repeatedly until they figure them out, but that's not me. Wo Long 2 is more than happy to teach you its ways without holding your hand and making things trivial. Combat is fast, fluid, and satisfying. My hands-on session gave me plenty of information about its combat systems, and the tutorials are considerably more useful than simply throwing a paragraph of text at you before sending you off to your untimely death. There's a lot to take in, but the game gradually explains how its different mechanics interact rather than expecting you to instinctively understand the entire combat system, and that made a huge difference when it came to my enjoyment. The most notable change is that rather…

title: Microsoft Reacts To Xbox Game Pass Rumor That Could Change The Service In A Big Way
description: Microsoft has released a statement in response to a new rumor that claims the company is considering a massive shakeup to Xbox Game Pass in 2027 that would include numerous significant changes. ResetEra user Slayven, who has accurately reported on unannounced Xbox news before, said the changes could include the bifurcation of Game Pass into two tiers: one with ads and one without. The tier with ads would be $13/month, while Game Pass without ads would cost $20/month, according to the report. Xbox Game Pass could see a big shakeup. That's $3/month less than Game Pass Ultimate currently, and the price cut is reportedly reflective of another big change: Microsoft is reportedly removing day-one new releases from Game Pass starting in the February-April window of 2027. The rumor also stated that cloud-streaming access is being taken out of Game Pass, but people can pay for a $6 add-on that gets you 25 hours. Additionally, the report said a Family Plan will be available for an extra $6/month. Beyond all of this, the report claimed there will be a tier of Game Pass that costs $15/month, and for that, people will get access to select titles in the Game Pass library, along with online multiplayer. Finally, it was reported that Microsoft will also offer a $11/month membership that provides access to online multiplayer alone. Microsoft responded to the rumor in a statement to GameSpot, originally obtained by Paul Tassi of Forbes. The statement reads: "We regularly test different Game Pass offerings and look at what works best for players in different markets. We don’t have any changes to announce today or plans that have been finalized. There are no changes to previously announced games coming to Game Pass Ultimate on day one." Not a random leaker Reputable leaker NateTheHate said on ResetEra that Slayven has a track record for accuracy, at least somewhat, so "the individual giving them information clearly has knowledge of some matters." However, NateTheHate did not…

title: James Pond Legacy Situation Is More Than Meets The AI
description: Last month, System 3 Software released a trailer for James Pond Legacy, a four-game collection for Nintendo Switch 2. But the gameplay footage was largely overshadowed by accusations its developer used generative AI to create the game's promotional artwork and cover. System 3 followed this trailer up with a blog post asserting that generative AI was not used in the development process for James Pond Legacy, but some wires were evidently crossed. If you go back and watch that trailer, it's not difficult to see why viewers pointed out the AI-like quality of the 3D characters adorning the game's box art and other promotional material. When System 3 responded to the accusations with the assertion that "no generative AI was used in the creation of the artwork," referring specifically to the Bovine Bomber character, this was based on the information it was given at the time by Antstream, the studio that handled the collection's actual development. "That was the statement that we were given at the time by Antstream," System 3 CEO Mark Cale told GameSpot during a call. "We weren't involved in the process. They supplied all of the artwork and they supplied, in the process, the [work-in-progress] illustration. All of that was given to us." Cale later provided GameSpot with the statement it received back in December from Antstream, well before the trailer was made public. "The art pipeline on some non-in-game assets includes algorithm-assisted depth and form translation: Original 2D concepts are input into a model to estimate volume and lighting, producing pseudo-3D drafts," reads the statement from Antstream. "Artists then manually repaint, re-render, and finalise all illustrations using this pipeline. The final assets are fully human-authored, with algorithms used only for intermediate visualisation." You may notice that the statement omits the term "AI," which led to some internal confusion. "We requested this [statement] for use across the board, including Steam, and to…

title: The Last Of Us Season 3 Is Probably The Final Season, HBO Says Yet Again
description: HBO boss Casey Bloys has once again said that the upcoming third season of The Last of Us is expected to be its last. He told Deadline that Season 3 is coming in 2027, though did not confirm when in the year. Asked if he still think it's the final season, Bloys said he believes showrunner Craig Mazin "has planned it as the final season." In January this year, Bloys was asked if Season 3 is going to be the last, and he said, "It certainly seems that way." However, at the time, Bloys admitted that a decision like that would come down to Mazin. Before this, Mazin said that Season 4 was essential to bring the show to a conclusion. However, Bloys has indicated that the show may wrap up its run with Season 3, which could be a longer season. “Craig is still working it out whether it will be two more seasons or one more long season. It hasn’t been decided yet, and I’m following Craig’s lead on that,” Bloys said in 2025. In a big shift for the series, franchise creator Naughty Dog is not involved creatively in Season 3, and Neil Druckmann dropped out as a writer/director. People have speculated about what this could mean, but Druckmann, for his part, said he left the show to focus on his work on Naughty Dog's games. He is currently directing Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and if it's true that Naughty Dog is also making The Last of Us 3, he's probably involved in that, too.

title: Dredge Has Never Been Cheaper, So Grab This Lovecraftian Fishing Adventure At An All-Time Low
description: Sometimes, I simply enjoy reeling people into playing a delightful indie, and Dredge … well, Dredge is one of those times. It’s a fishing game, yes, but it’s one that hides a Lovecraftian selection of horrors beneath the surface of what, at first, seems fairly tame. If you’re not quite ready for the sheer panic of the best horror games but still want something with spooky vibes, Dredge is what you’re looking for, and right now, it’s cheaper than ever. As someone who doesn’t like the idea of fishing, it surprised me that Dredge ended up becoming one of my favorite indie games. That’s helped by the fact that it’s not really about fishing, at least not in the traditional sense. Instead, it’s about making your boat better with your spoils and eventually finding the courage to head out at night. And trust me, you’ll want to brave it. At the beginning, going out in the dark is a good way to lose. As you experience the story of this interesting world, you’ll inevitably find ways to make trips that were once too dangerous, while also gaining the ability to travel farther and visit different towns. Even during the day, there are still risks, but nothing compares to the horrors you’ll encounter once the sun goes down. The more you let your panic rise, the more likely you are to see deadly creatures, like a phantom shark or a giant crab disguised as a shipwreck. There have been plenty of times when I’ve driven my little ship as fast as possible to avoid enemies, and in reality, the tension and panic rushing through my body have been surprisingly high, considering I’m used to playing horror games and watching scary movies. Dredge is one of those indies that, if you’re even somewhat intrigued by the premise, you need to give it a try. There are very few indies—or games in general—that manage to blend something I’d find truly boring with a world that is genuinely interesting, then somehow make the two fit together. Dredge is a truly solid experience, and while the opening is a…

title: Paradox's grand strategy game Afterworld hasn't got a fixed history, it changes with every playthrough
description: Each time you start a new campaign in Afterworld, Paradox's upcoming post-apocalyptic grand strategy game, a tiny virtual historian cracks their knuckles and gets to work writing a new 200-year history for what happened to North America in the dying days of the great war. They will decide where the great powers fired their nuclear-tipped missiles, where they released their clouds of flesh-eating nanites, where they dropped their lung-bubbling chemical weapons, and they will decide who survived and who died. These procedural changes should mean that each time you start a new game of Afterworld, the map will be dramatically different from the last. That flexibility to rewrite the surface of Afterworld is vital, game director Dan Lind tells me, "Otherwise it undermines a lot of the exploration". Read more
